Package bakerydms

Class DatabaseConnector

  • java.lang.Object
    • bakerydms.DatabaseConnector
  • public class DatabaseConnector
extends java.lang.Object
    Connects the program to the user's MySQL database.

    Nothing about the database's location or login is written in the code. The user types the server address, port, database name, username and password in BakeryOrderWindow, and this class:

    1. checks every value with validate(String, String, String, String, char[]),
    2. builds the JDBC connection string by concatenation with buildUrl(String, int, String),
    3. opens the connection and checks that the orders table exists, and
    4. returns a MySqlOrderRepository for OrderManager to use.
    Any failure (wrong password, MySQL not running, database missing) is thrown as a DataAccessException with a plain-English message. This class needs the MySQL Connector/J driver on the classpath.

    Usage: 

    
 DatabaseConnector connector = new DatabaseConnector();
 OrderRepository database = connector.connect("localhost", "3306", "bakery_dms",
         "root", passwordTypedByUser);
 int orderCount = manager.connectTo(database);
    Version:
    4.0 (Phase 4, Module 11)
    Author:
    Kayla Ewing
    See Also:
    MySqlOrderRepository

      • validate

        public java.util.List<java.lang.String> validate​(java.lang.String host,
                                                 java.lang.String portText,
                                                 java.lang.String database,
                                                 java.lang.String username,
                                                 char[] password)
        Checks the connection details the user typed, before trying to connect.
        Parameters:
        host - server address, e.g. localhost or 127.0.0.1 (may include ":port")
        portText - port number as typed (blank means 3306)
        database - database name, e.g. bakery_dms
        username - MySQL username
        password - MySQL password (may be blank: some accounts have none)
        Returns:
        a list of problems; an EMPTY list means the details look valid
